NCERT Ex 9.1 Q1 Easy 2 Marks
Q. A circus artist is climbing a 20 m long rope, which is tightly stretched and tied from the top of a vertical pole to the ground. Find the height of the pole, if the angle made by the rope with the ground level is 30°.
GIVENAB is the pole, AC is the rope (hypotenuse) = 20 m, angle of rope with ground, ∠ACB = 30°, right angled at B
FORMULAsinθ = Opposite sideHypotenuse
WORKING In △ABC, right-angled at B:
sin C = ABAC

sin 30° = AB20
12 = AB20 [sin 30° = 1/2]

AB = 20 × 12
AB = 102021 [cancelling a common factor of 2]
∴ AB = 10
ANSWER∴ Height of the pole = 10 m
NCERT Ex 9.1 Q2 Medium 3 Marks
Q. A tree breaks due to storm and the broken part bends so that the top of the tree touches the ground making an angle 30° with it. The distance between the foot of the tree to the point where the top touches the ground is 8 m. Find the height of the tree.
GIVENA is the foot of the tree, AB is the standing (unbroken) part, BC is the broken part, C is the point where the top touches the ground, AC = 8 m, ∠ACB = 30°, right angled at A
FORMULAtanθ = Opposite sideAdjacent side; Pythagoras theorem: (Hypotenuse)² = (Base)² + (Perpendicular)²
WORKING In △ABC, right-angled at A:
tan C = ABAC

tan 30° = AB8
1√3 = AB8 [tan 30° = 1/√3]

AB = 8√3 m

By Pythagoras theorem in △ABC:
BC² = AB² + AC²

BC² = 8√3² + 8²
BC² = 643 + 64

Taking LCM:
BC² = 643 + 1923 [LCM of 3 and 1 is 3]
BC² = 2563

BC = √2563
BC = 16√3 m

Height of tree = AB + BC
Height of tree = 8√3 + 16√3
Height of tree = 24√3

Rationalising the denominator:
Height of tree = 24√3 × √3√3
Height of tree = 24 × √3√3 × √3
Height of tree = 824√331 [cancelling a common factor of 3]
∴ Height of tree = 8√3
ANSWER∴ Height of the tree = 8√3 m
NCERT Ex 9.1 Q3 Medium 3 Marks
Q. A contractor plans to install two slides for the children to play in a park. For the children below the age of 5 years, she prefers to have a slide whose top is at a height of 1.5 m, and is inclined at an angle of 30° to the ground, whereas for elder children, she wants to have a steep slide at a height of 3 m, and inclined at an angle of 60° to the ground. What should be the length of the slide in each case?
GIVENSlide 1: height AB = 32 m, angle with ground ∠ACB = 30°
Slide 2: height DE = 3 m, angle with ground ∠DFE = 60°
Both right angled at the foot of the vertical height
FORMULAsinθ = Opposite sideHypotenuse
WORKING Slide 1:
In △ABC, right-angled at B:
sin C = ABAC

sin 30° = 3/2AC
12 = 3/2AC [sin 30° = 1/2]

AC = 32 × 2
∴ AC = 3

Slide 2:
In △DEF, right-angled at E:
sin F = DEDF

sin 60° = 3DF
√32 = 3DF [sin 60° = √3/2]

DF = 3 × 2√3
DF = 6√3

Rationalising the denominator:
DF = 6√3 × √3√3
DF = 6 × √3√3 × √3
DF = 26√331 [cancelling a common factor of 3]
∴ DF = 2√3
ANSWER∴ Length of slide for children below 5 years = 3 m; length of slide for elder children = 2√3 m
NCERT Ex 9.1 Q4 Easy 2 Marks
Q. The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point on the ground, which is 30 m away from the foot of the tower, is 30°. Find the height of the tower.
GIVENAB is the tower, C is the point on the ground, AC = 30 m, angle of elevation ∠ACB = 30°, right angled at A
FORMULAtanθ = Opposite sideAdjacent side
WORKING In △ABC, right-angled at A:
tan C = ABAC

tan 30° = AB30
1√3 = AB30 [tan 30° = 1/√3]

AB = 30√3

Rationalising the denominator:
AB = 30√3 × √3√3
AB = 30 × √3√3 × √3
AB = 1030√331 [cancelling a common factor of 3]
∴ AB = 10√3
ANSWER∴ Height of the tower = 10√3 m
NCERT Ex 9.1 Q5 Medium 3 Marks
Q. A kite is flying at a height of 60 m above the ground. The string attached to the kite is temporarily tied to a point on the ground. The inclination of the string with the ground is 60°. Find the length of the string, assuming that there is no slack in the string.
GIVENA is the position of the kite, B is the point directly below it on the ground, C is the point where the string is tied, AB = 60 m, ∠ACB = 60°, right angled at B
FORMULAsinθ = Opposite sideHypotenuse
WORKING In △ABC, right-angled at B:
sin C = ABAC

sin 60° = 60AC
√32 = 60AC [sin 60° = √3/2]

AC = 60 × 2√3
AC = 120√3

Rationalising the denominator:
AC = 120√3 × √3√3
AC = 120 × √3√3 × √3
AC = 40120√331 [cancelling a common factor of 3]
∴ AC = 40√3
ANSWER∴ Length of the string = 40√3 m
NCERT Ex 9.1 Q6 Hard 4 Marks
Q. A 1.5 m tall boy is standing at some distance from a 30 m tall building. The angle of elevation from his eyes to the top of the building increases from 30° to 60° as he walks towards the building. Find the distance he walked towards the building.
GIVENCD is the building = 30 m, E is the point on CD at the boy's eye level, A and B are the boy's first and second positions on the horizontal through E, boy's height = 32 m, ∠DAE = 30°, ∠DBE = 60°, right angled at E
FORMULAtanθ = Opposite sideAdjacent side
WORKING DE = CD − boy's height
DE = 30 − 32
DE = 602 − 32 [taking LCM]
DE = 572

In △DEA, right-angled at E:
tan A = DEEA

tan 30° = 57/2EA
1√3 = 57/2EA [tan 30° = 1/√3]

EA = 572 × √3
EA = 57√32

In △DEB, right-angled at E:
tan B = DEEB

tan 60° = 57/2EB
√3 = 57/2EB [tan 60° = √3]

EB = 572 × 1√3
EB = 57 × 12 × √3
EB = 572√3

Rationalising the denominator:
EB = 572√3 × √3√3
EB = 57 × √32 × 3
EB = 57√36
EB = 1957√362 [cancelling a common factor of 3]

Distance walked = EA − EB
Distance walked = 57√32 − 19√32
Distance walked = 57√3 − 19√32
Distance walked = 38√32
Distance walked = 1938√321 [cancelling a common factor of 2]
∴ Distance walked = 19√3
ANSWER∴ Distance walked by the boy towards the building = 19√3 m
NCERT Ex 9.1 Q7 Medium 3 Marks
Q. From a point on the ground, the angles of elevation of the bottom and the top of a transmission tower fixed at the top of a 20 m high building are 45° and 60° respectively. Find the height of the tower.
GIVENAB is the building = 20 m (A = foot, B = top of building = foot of tower), BD is the tower, C is the point on the ground, ∠BCA = 45°, ∠DCA = 60°, right angled at A
FORMULAtanθ = Opposite sideAdjacent side
WORKING In △ABC, right-angled at A:
tan C = ABAC

tan 45° = 20AC
1 = 20AC [tan 45° = 1]
∴ AC = 20

In △ADC, right-angled at A:
tan C = ADAC
tan C = AB + BDAC

tan 60° = 20 + BD20
√3 = 20 + BD20 [tan 60° = √3]

20√3 = 20 + BD
∴ BD = 20√3 − 20
∴ BD = 20(√3 − 1)
ANSWER∴ Height of the tower = 20(√3 − 1) m
NCERT Ex 9.1 Q8 Hard 4 Marks
Q. A statue, 1.6 m tall, stands on the top of a pedestal. From a point on the ground, the angle of elevation of the top of the statue is 60° and from the same point the angle of elevation of the top of the pedestal is 45°. Find the height of the pedestal.
GIVENBC is the pedestal (B = foot, C = top of pedestal = foot of statue), CD is the statue = 85 m, A is the point on the ground, ∠CAB = 45°, ∠DAB = 60°, right angled at B
FORMULAtanθ = Opposite sideAdjacent side
WORKING In △ABC, right-angled at B:
tan A = BCAB

tan 45° = BCAB
1 = BCAB [tan 45° = 1]
∴ AB = BC

In △ABD, right-angled at B:
tan A = BDAB
tan A = BC + CDAB

tan 60° = BC + 8/5BC [since AB = BC]
√3 = BC + 8/5BC

√3 × BC = BC + 85
√3 × BC − BC = 85
BC(√3 − 1) = 85

BC = 8/5√3 − 1
BC = 85(√3 − 1)

Rationalising the denominator:
BC = 85(√3 − 1) × √3 + 1√3 + 1
BC = 8(√3 + 1)5(3 − 1) [(√3−1)(√3+1) = 3−1]
BC = 8(√3 + 1)10
BC = 48(√3 + 1)105 [cancelling a common factor of 2]
∴ BC = 4(√3 + 1)5
ANSWER∴ Height of the pedestal = 4(√3 + 1)5 m
NCERT Ex 9.1 Q9 Medium 3 Marks
Q. The angle of elevation of the top of a building from the foot of the tower is 30° and the angle of elevation of the top of the tower from the foot of the building is 60°. If the tower is 50 m high, find the height of the building.
GIVENAB is the tower = 50 m (A = top, B = foot), CD is the building (C = top, D = foot), ∠ADB = 60°, ∠DBC = 30°, right angled at B and D respectively
FORMULAtanθ = Opposite sideAdjacent side
WORKING In △ABD, right-angled at B:
tan D = ABBD

tan 60° = 50BD
√3 = 50BD [tan 60° = √3]
∴ BD = 50√3

In △BCD, right-angled at D:
tan B = DCBD

tan 30° = DC50/√3
1√3 = DC50/√3 [tan 30° = 1/√3]

DC = 50√3 × 1√3
DC = 50 × 1√3 × √3
DC = 503
ANSWER∴ Height of the building = 503 m
NCERT Ex 9.1 Q10 Hard 4 Marks
Q. Two poles of equal heights are standing opposite each other on either side of the road, which is 80 m wide. From a point between them on the road, the angles of elevation of the top of the poles are 60° and 30° respectively. Find the height of the poles and the distances of the point from the poles.
GIVENAB and CD are the two poles of equal height h, BD = 80 m is the width of the road, P is a point on BD with BP = x and PD = 80 − x, ∠APB = 60°, ∠CPD = 30°, both right angled at B and D respectively
FORMULAtanθ = Opposite sideAdjacent side
WORKING In △ABP, right-angled at B:
tan P = ABBP

tan 60° = hx
√3 = hx [tan 60° = √3]
∴ h = x√3   …(1)

In △CDP, right-angled at D:
tan P = CDDP

tan 30° = h80 − x
1√3 = h80 − x [tan 30° = 1/√3]
∴ h = 80 − x√3   …(2)

From (1) and (2):
x√3 = 80 − x√3
x√3 × √3 = 80 − x
3x = 80 − x
3x + x = 80
4x = 80
∴ x = 20

Substituting x = 20 in (1):
h = 20√3
PD = 80 − x
PD = 80 − 20
∴ PD = 60
ANSWER∴ Height of the poles = 20√3 m; distance of the point from the first pole = 20 m and from the second pole = 60 m
NCERT Ex 9.1 Q11 Hard 4 Marks
Q. A TV tower stands vertically on a bank of a canal. From a point on the other bank directly opposite the tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is 60°. From another point 20 m away from this point on the same bank, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is 30°. Find the height of the tower and the width of the canal.
GIVENAB is the tower (height h), C is the point on the opposite bank directly across from the tower, BC = x is the width of the canal, D is 20 m further from C, ∠ACB = 60°, ∠ADB = 30°, right angled at B
FORMULAtanθ = Opposite sideAdjacent side
WORKING In △ABC, right-angled at B:
tan C = ABBC

tan 60° = hx
√3 = hx [tan 60° = √3]
∴ h = x√3   …(1)

In △ABD, right-angled at B:
tan D = ABBD
tan D = hx + 20

tan 30° = hx + 20
1√3 = hx + 20 [tan 30° = 1/√3]
∴ h = x + 20√3   …(2)

From (1) and (2):
x√3 = x + 20√3
x√3 × √3 = x + 20
3x = x + 20
3x − x = 20
2x = 20
∴ x = 10

Substituting x = 10 in (1):
h = 10√3
ANSWER∴ Height of the tower = 10√3 m; width of the canal = 10 m
NCERT Ex 9.1 Q12 Hard 4 Marks
Q. From the top of a 7 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a cable tower is 60°, and the angle of depression of its foot is 45°. Determine the height of the tower.
GIVENAB is the building = 7 m (A = top, B = foot), CD is the cable tower (C = foot, D = top), E is the point on CD level with A, angle of depression of C from A = 45°, angle of elevation of D from A = 60°
FORMULAtanθ = Opposite sideAdjacent side; alternate angles are equal for a horizontal line of sight and a horizontal ground line
WORKING Angle of depression = angle of elevation [alternate angles, AE horizontal]
∴ ∠ACB = 45°

In △ABC, right-angled at B:
tan C = ABBC

tan 45° = 7BC
1 = 7BC [tan 45° = 1]
∴ BC = 7

AE = BC = 7  [ABCE is a rectangle]
CE = AB = 7

In △AED, right-angled at E:
tan A = EDAE
tan A = CD − CEAE

tan 60° = CD − 77
√3 = CD − 77 [tan 60° = √3]

7√3 = CD − 7
∴ CD = 7√3 + 7
∴ CD = 7(√3 + 1)
ANSWER∴ Height of the tower = 7(√3 + 1) m
NCERT Ex 9.1 Q13 Medium 3 Marks
Q. As observed from the top of a 75 m high lighthouse from the sea level, the angles of depression of two ships are 30° and 45°. If one ship is exactly behind the other on the same side of the lighthouse, find the distance between the two ships.
GIVENAB is the lighthouse = 75 m (A = top, B = foot at sea level), C is the nearer ship (angle of depression 45°), D is the farther ship (angle of depression 30°), C lies between B and D, right angled at B
FORMULAtanθ = Opposite sideAdjacent side; alternate angles are equal
WORKING Angle of depression = angle of elevation [alternate angles]
∠ACB = 45°
∠ADB = 30°

In △ABC, right-angled at B:
tan C = ABBC

tan 45° = 75BC
1 = 75BC [tan 45° = 1]
∴ BC = 75

In △ABD, right-angled at B:
tan D = ABBD

tan 30° = 75BD
1√3 = 75BD [tan 30° = 1/√3]
∴ BD = 75√3

CD = BD − BC
CD = 75√3 − 75
∴ CD = 75(√3 − 1)
ANSWER∴ Distance between the two ships = 75(√3 − 1) m
NCERT Ex 9.1 Q14 Hard 4 Marks
Q. A 1.2 m tall girl spots a balloon moving with the wind in a horizontal line at a height of 88.2 m from the ground. The angle of elevation of the balloon from the eyes of the girl at any instant is 60°. After some time, the angle of elevation reduces to 30°. Find the distance travelled by the balloon during the interval.
GIVENP is the balloon's first position, Q is the balloon's second position, A is the point at the girl's eye level, E and F are points directly below P and Q on the horizontal through A, girl's height = 1.2 m, height of balloon = 88.2 m, ∠PAE = 60°, ∠QAF = 30°, right angled at E and F respectively
FORMULAtanθ = Opposite sideAdjacent side
WORKING Height of balloon above eye level = 4415 − 65 [88.2 = 441/5, 1.2 = 6/5]
Height of balloon above eye level = 4355
Height of balloon above eye level = 8743551 [cancelling a common factor of 5]
∴ Height of balloon above eye level = 87

In △APE, right-angled at E:
tan A = PEAE

tan 60° = 87AE
√3 = 87AE [tan 60° = √3]
AE = 87√3

Rationalising the denominator:
AE = 87√3 × √3√3
AE = 87 × √3√3 × √3
AE = 87√33
AE = 2987√331 [cancelling a common factor of 3]
∴ AE = 29√3

In △AQF, right-angled at F:
tan A = QFAF

tan 30° = 87AF
1√3 = 87AF [tan 30° = 1/√3]
∴ AF = 87√3

Distance travelled = AF − AE
Distance travelled = 87√3 − 29√3
∴ Distance travelled = 58√3
ANSWER∴ Distance travelled by the balloon = 58√3 m
NCERT Ex 9.1 Q15 Hard 5 Marks
Q. A straight highway leads to the foot of a tower. A man standing at the top of the tower observes a car at an angle of depression of 30°, which is approaching the foot of the tower with a uniform speed. Six seconds later, the angle of depression of the car is found to be 60°. Find the time taken by the car to reach the foot of the tower from this point.
GIVENAB is the tower (height h), D is the car's initial position (angle of depression 30°), C is the car's position 6 seconds later (angle of depression 60°), right angled at B, car moves with uniform speed
FORMULAtanθ = Opposite sideAdjacent side; alternate angles are equal; Speed = DistanceTime
WORKING Angle of depression = angle of elevation [alternate angles]
∠ADB = 30°
∠ACB = 60°

In △ABD, right-angled at B:
tan D = ABBD

tan 30° = hBD
1√3 = hBD [tan 30° = 1/√3]
∴ BD = h√3

In △ABC, right-angled at B:
tan C = ABBC

tan 60° = hBC
√3 = hBC [tan 60° = √3]
∴ BC = h√3

Distance covered in 6 seconds = CD
CD = BD − BC
CD = h√3 − h√3
CD = 3h − h√3 [taking LCM]
CD = 2h√3

Speed = DistanceTime
Speed = 2h/√36
Speed = 2h√3 × 6
Speed = 2h6√3
Speed = 12h63√3 [cancelling a common factor of 2]
Speed = h3√3

Remaining distance to the foot of the tower = BC = h√3

Time = DistanceSpeed
Time = h/√3h/(3√3)
Time = h√3 × 3√3h
Time = h × 3√3√3 × h
Time = 3√3√3 [h cancels from top and bottom]
∴ Time = 3
ANSWER∴ The car takes 3 seconds to reach the foot of the tower
Angle of Elevation and Depression ▾
Angle of elevation: the angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal, when the object being viewed is above the horizontal level of the eye.

Angle of depression: the angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal, when the object being viewed is below the horizontal level of the eye.

The line of sight is the line drawn from the eye of an observer to the point on the object being viewed.
Trigonometric Ratios of an Acute Angle ▾
For an acute angle θ in a right triangle:

sinθ = Opposite sideHypotenuse

cosθ = Adjacent sideHypotenuse

tanθ = Opposite sideAdjacent side
Standard Angle Values ▾
θ0°30°45°60°90°
sinθ0121√2√321
cosθ1√321√2120
tanθ01√31√3Not defined
Solving Heights & Distances Problems — Method ▾
1. Draw a labelled right-triangle diagram from the problem statement
2. Identify the right angle, the given side/angle, and the side to be found
3. Choose the trig ratio that connects the known side to the unknown side
4. Substitute the standard angle value and solve for the unknown
5. Rationalise the denominator if it contains a surd, and express the final answer as a simplified fraction or surd — never as a decimal
